title: Intervention runbook for LLM A/B-synced rollouts (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This document collects practical intervention scripts, communications, and quick triage checklists for experiments where multiple LLM-backed routes are turned on in lockstep (A/B-synced exposures, staggered cohorts). Focus is on: preventing user-visible regressions, limiting cost/latency shock, and preserving signal integrity for evaluation.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to features routed through Redwood Console (hosted & dedicated routes).
- Assumes available metrics: latency p50/p95, token spend per route, model fallback rate, hallucination-rate proxy (heuristic), and key business conversion signals.
- Not a replacement for full incident runbooks; this is for mid-experiment interventions and fast rollback patterns.

When to use this runbook (triggering conditions):
- Experiment latency p95 exceeds baseline + 300ms for 10m rolling window
- Token/unit spend for variant > 2x control over 1h without corresponding conversion lift
- Automated QA eval set drift score > threshold (see metrics mapping below)
- Human moderation alerts spike (>= 3 in 15m) for cohort exposed to variant
- Pager triggered for degraded customer SLA tied to model route

Primary stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Experiment Owner (product/PM): decide risk tolerance and approve exposure changes
- Oncall SRE / Serving Runtime: execute routing changes (Console toggles, traffic weights), check infra health
- Evaluation Lead (Applied ML): run quick evals on holdout prompt set, annotate results
- Comms Lead (Product Ops): draft user-facing message if rollback affects external users

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Capture current state: traffic partitioning, model versions, capacity pool ids, and recent deploys.
2) Verify automated metrics: compare p50/p95, error rate, token spend, and model fallback logs across slices.
3) Check infra alerts (GPU OOM, node restarts) — rapid correlation often reveals non-model root cause.
4) Run narrow synthetic probe: 5 prompt samples from the eval deck against both control and variant; record time and top-k differences.
5) If user complaints exist, tag representative sessions and extract full request/response for review (privacy-preserving filters applied).

Immediate interventions (ordered by reversibility):
- Safe quick-fallback: shift the variant’s traffic to a cheaper/older model variant (Console -> routing policy -> fallback) while keeping exposure percentage constant. This preserves experiment continuity and reduces risk.
- Slice quarantine (recommended for noisy cohorts): remove affected cohort slice from experiment routing and redirect to control. Good for cohort-specific behavioral anomalies.
- Throttle traffic: reduce variant exposure by 50% and observe 10–20 minutes. Avoid immediate 0% unless severe.
- Full rollback: set variant weight to 0% and deploy controlled revert message in runbook log. Use when safety signals or conversion loss exceed committed thresholds.

Step-by-step: shifting to fallback variant (example run):
- Identify compatible fallback model in catalog (must share same API schema).
- Console: create routing override for cohort id -> model: <fallback-id>. Version pin to stable commit.
- Monitor: p50/p95, token spend, and evaluation deck answers at 2m, 10m, 30m marks.
- Note: annotate the experiment record with timestamp and rationale (JIRA ticket).

Rollbacks: communication and postmortem quick template
- Immediate internal note (Slack): short reason, action taken, who acted, and link to JIRA. Example: "ACTION: reduced variant X -> 0% due to p95 latency spike +420ms. Acting: Dana. JIRA-3421."
- Customer-facing message (if external users impacted): short blameless note, expected timeline, work being done. Keep legal/security in loop if user PII or compliance surfaces.
- Postmortem skeleton: what happened, timeline, key signals, action taken, RCA (infra vs model vs data), follow-ups (experiments to run). Retro due within 5 business days.

Observability probes and synthetic suites (quick list):
- Latency probes: variable-length prompts (short conversational 20 tokens, long generation 600 tokens) run against control and variant every 2m when active.
- Quality probes: 40 prompts from curated evals covering factual QA, instruction following, and safety-sensitive cases. Simple scoring heuristic: token-level perplexity delta + heuristic hallucination flags.
- Cost probes: standardized prompt pair to estimate tokens-per-response and average generation length.

Metric mapping (what to watch and why):
- infra_latency_p95 (route-level): immediate signal of capacity problems
- tokens_per_request (route-level): drives cost shock and may indicate prompting differences
- model_fallback_rate (route-level): indicates model instability or runtime exceptions
- eval_deck_score_delta (experiment): quick quality regression check
- moderation_alert_count (cohort): safety regression proxy
- business_conversion_rate (experiment-level): downstream business impact

Communication templates (short)
- Internal: "[ACTION] Reduced exposure for experiment X to 25% due to increased p95 latency (+320ms). Monitoring 30m window. Owner: Priya. Link: JIRA-3421"
- Customer (if needed): "We temporarily reduced an experimental AI feature while we investigate slower-than-expected responses. No user data was exposed. Expect update within 24 hours."

Checklist for resuming exposure (preconditions):
- Synthetic probes show p95 within baseline + 100ms for 60m
- Eval deck quality delta recovered to within pre-commit threshold
- SRE confirms no infra anomalies for relevant capacity pool
- Product lead signs off on re-run plan and safety mitigations (rate limits, user opt-out)

Notes and best-practice heuristics (ops heuristics):
- Prefer progressive throttles over hard kills to preserve signal for evaluation but limit user harm.
- When cost is the driver: consider a model configuration change (quantization/shorter context) rather than immediate rollback.
- Keep experiment tags enriched with cohort and slice metadata — makes quarantine surgical.
- For multi-model chest exposure (simultaneous A/B for two model families), consider asymmetric rollback (reduce heavier model first).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Automate synthetic probe runner into Console so we get auto-snapshots on every exposure change (Ethan owning spike).
- Define exact hallucination proxy threshold for urgent rollback (APPLY ML to propose).
- Add an audit automation to surface non-owner rollouts older than 48h to product ops.

Appendix: quick commands & scribbles (not authoritative)
- Console routing quick steps: Routing -> New override -> select cohort -> set model id -> save and annotate
- Quick JIRA template: SUMMARY: Rollback experiment X; ACTION: set weight 0%; WHY: p95 latency + token spike; OWNER: <name>
- Slack shortcuts: @oncall-sre, @eval-team, #rollout-ops

Notes to self: keep this lean — heavier procedural content belongs in experiment-specific runbooks. This doc should be the "what to do fast" sheet for cross-functional rollouts that are A/B-synced.

References and related pages:
- CONFLUENCE: AB-Sync run cookbook (link above)
- JIRA-3421: current incident ticket for the January trial
- Experimental signal catalogue: see product-console/signal-lexicon (pending import)
